label: copy steps 2-3 of length-3 sequences (recall_idx 1,2 when L=3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase of the shortest sequences (L=3): at t=4 and t=5 (outputting original tokens 1 and 2, i.e. the last two outputs). L=3 holds 97% of activation mass; L=4 copy-end steps contribute ~3% and longer sequences almost nothing. Never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on the first copy output (recall_idx 0). Within L=3 it is gated by the fed-back input token: high rate for b,g,i,j,q,y and digits 1-3, near-zero for d,m,t,v,w (excluded), intermediate for others. Magnitude is larger at t=5 (prev2 = <DEL>, 62% of mass) than t=4, and top activations are on input g. Plain (L==3)&(t>=4) gives dev F1 0.72 / mass recall 0.97; the token exclusion raises precision to 0.70 (F1 0.79).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=6: g, 0, y, r; t=12: g, 0, y, i; t=4: g, y, q, 0) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: j, g, c, 0; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
